n: Whenever God tried to heal Israel, more sin came to light. Samaria, the capital, was full of deceit, burglary, and street robbery.

f.w: When I would have healed Israel

f.g: Capital city of the northern kingdom.

n: They never stop to think that God remembers all their evil. Their deeds now surround them, in full view of God.

f.w: they consider not in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness

n: Court officials entertain the king with wickedness and lies. Corruption flows from the top down.
They are all burning with passion like a baker’s oven, so hot the baker doesn’t even need to stoke it while the dough rises. Their plotting smolders constantly.

f.w: as an oven heated by the baker
f.g: Ancient ovens were kept smoldering overnight and stoked to full heat in the morning.

n: On the king’s festival day, the officials get him drunk and he joins hands with mockers—setting the stage for a coup.
Their hearts smolder with intrigue all night like an oven; by morning, the plot blazes into action.
Hot like ovens, they consume their rulers; king after king falls. In Hosea’s day, four of Israel’s last six kings were assassinated—yet no one calls on God.

f.w: there is none among them that calleth unto me

n: Ephraim mixes with the nations—adopting foreign ways and alliances. He is like a flat cake burned on one side and raw on the other: half-baked and useless.

f.g: Bread cooked on hot stones had to be flipped; unturned, it was charred and doughy.

n: Foreigners drain his strength, but he doesn’t notice. Gray hairs appear, but he doesn’t realize he’s growing old and weak. Spiritual decline can be gradual and unnoticed.

f.w: gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not

n: Israel’s pride testifies against it; despite everything, they will not return to the Lord.

f.w: the pride of Israel testifieth to his face

n: Ephraim is like a silly, senseless dove, flitting back and forth between Egypt and Assyria for help instead of trusting God. Israel’s last kings did exactly this.

f.g: A naive, easily misled dove; “heart” = sense.

f.w: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria

n: As they fly about, God will throw a net over them and bring them down like birds. Their schemes will catch them.

f.w: I will spread my net upon them

f.g: As they were warned in their assembly.

n: Woe to them! They fled from God and rebelled. He longs to redeem them, but they slander Him.
They wail on their beds but don’t cry to God from the heart. They gather to plead for grain and wine (perhaps through pagan rites) but turn away from Him.

f.w: they have not cried unto me with their heart
they assemble themselves for corn and wine
f.g: Some manuscripts read “they gash themselves,” a pagan practice to win rain.

n: God trained and strengthened them like a coach, yet they plot evil against Him.
They turn, but not upward to the Most High—like a faulty bow that misses its mark. Their leaders will fall for their arrogant words, and Egypt will mock them.

f.g: A warped bow that cannot shoot straight.
